artist.name: Alexander 23
artist.short_description: American singer-songwriter and producer whose sparse emotional pop connects vulnerability with studio craftsmanship.
artist.biography: Alexander 23 is the performing name of Alexander Glantz, an American singer-songwriter and producer raised in Deerfield, Illinois. After developing his musical skills and working in Los Angeles, he began releasing his own music in 2019, starting with 'Dirty AF1s' and the EP 'I'm Sorry I Love You'. His 2020 song 'IDK You Yet' became an important breakthrough, arriving during the pandemic and circulating widely through social media. His second EP, 'Oh No, Not Again!', followed in 2021 and included 'Cry Over Boys'. He has described that song as an examination of putting romantic fantasies ahead of personal wellbeing. Alongside his solo releases, Alexander developed a substantial production and songwriting career. The Recording Academy has documented his work with other popular artists, including contributions to Olivia Rodrigo's music. His first full-length album, 'Aftershock', appeared in July 2022 and included 'Hate Me If It Helps' and 'The Hardest Part'. In interviews he has explained the conflicting feelings in the former and the sensitive grief surrounding the latter. Afterglow places his solo work in the emotional-pop and alternative singer-songwriter space as an editorial description. His profile is a particularly useful discovery link to Chelsea Cutler, with whom he has a documented recording collaboration.
